title: Anthropic confirms it is circulating a draft federal AI bill; spokesperson: it 'requires frontier developers to test ... submit them to independent evaluation'
quote_verbatim: It requires frontier developers to test the most powerful models, be transparent to the public about their findings, submit them to independent evaluation
what_is_new: RTHK says Anthropic has confirmed it is circulating the draft among US lawmakers, and quotes the company saying the proposal 'grants the federal government the ability to block or deter dangerous deployments'.
why_for_agiright: Major-company statement within 48h on evaluation independence and the government's power to block models; confirms the run-9 draft-bill lead.
doubts: Statement relayed by agencies (RTHK credits 'Agencies'); no Anthropic primary found (anthropic.com/news newest item Oct 15; guessed policy URL 404). Rated A as a major-company statement; the parent may downgrade to B because it's secondary. Published 05:58Z, before this run's window start (~12:00Z Oct 17) but not logged in run 9. Topic-328 already notes a spokesperson comment to Politico. RTHK also says Anthropic wrote in June that 'absent a strong federal law, states should retain full authority to legislate'; the draft preempts some state rules (2026-10-18-009). Not reconciled.

title: India Today: Anthropic spokesperson calls the draft's measures 'sensible policies we believe Congress should act on'; says it reflects the Advanced AI Framework

Its paraphrase that government evaluators would have to inform Commerce within 72 hours differs from aipolicy.tech, which says the independent evaluator does. Not reconciled. Consistent with @ashleyrgold's account (X item in this file).
